messages:
mike.ae: Kicking off a POC with AquilaEdge — they want to run classification + summarization on clinical notes. They shipped a forked Llama-3-13B variant with a custom tokenizer + LoRA adapters. Need a quick compatibility + pricing triage: KV cache layout, supported quantization (nf4/int8), tokenizer conversion risk, KMS for customer-managed keys, and latency SLOs. cc @tara.se @anita.sec @devon.infra

tara.se: Thanks — can you share the model artifact link and a few sample input size stats? LoRA presence means we can either bake adapters or apply at runtime; both have tradeoffs. Do they include tokenizer.json and merges/vocab?

mike.ae: Artifact: https://files.aquilaedge.io/models/aq-llama3-13b-v2.tar.gz
median doc ~3k tokens, typical 128-generation, max observed 28k tokens. Throughput target ~600 reqs/min, 95p latency target <300ms for short prompts.

devon.infra: 28k context is big — runtime needs long-context kernels and KV sharding. For <300ms we'd need optimized kernels + persistent KV layout. If they require runtime LoRA, memory & KV overhead increases. Also need to know if the tokenizer changes tokenization density (might blow up token counts).

anita.sec: Security: external weights + custom code -> license and supply-chain review. We need SBOM and confirmation adapters don't load exec code at runtime. KMS with customer keys ok but ops needs onboarding and attestation. If they process PHI, legal needs BAA before we accept data.

tara.se: On tokenizer: if they can export HF-style tokenizer.json + vocab we can convert cleanly. Tokenizer mismatch can change embeddings/regression; advise adding a small eval set to verify. For LoRA: baking at compile time reduces runtime complexity but may require retracing; runtime adapters keep flexibility but increases token memory.

mike.ae: They ran nf4 and int8 locally with speedups ~3.5x on infer-only. Any runtime compatibility caveats for nf4 on A100? They also want Redwood to use their CMK in our KMS.

devon.infra: nf4 on A100 is supported in our runtime path; int8 needs calibration runs and can change logits slightly. Ensure they provide calibration dataset or run our cal script. For KV cache: our runtime expects per-head interleaved KV shapes; their LoRA must not change kv shape. Ask them to run this quick check and paste shapes:

```python
# sanity check snippet for them to run
import torch
# run a forward pass and print kv shapes from the attention cache
print('kv_shapes:', kv.keys(), [v.shape for v in kv.values()])
```

lucy.salesops: Pricing: rough reserved estimate for a 4xA100 dedicated pool (99.9% SLO, burst to 6 GPUs) ~ $25k/month. Hosted PAYG for long-context workloads ramps token-based billing — will propose two options (reserved vs burstable). I’ll finalize numbers once infra provides perf curves.

anita.sec: Also need completed security questionnaire, data retention policy, and copy of their license. If they insist on running with customer data, we need to confirm retention and deletion SLA. Flagging legal for DPA + BAA if PHI.

tara.se: Action items (short):
1) mike.ae: upload artifact + tokenizer + license (and sample eval prompts)
2) aquila: run kv-shape snippet & provide LoRA format (peft? fused?)
3) devon.infra: estimate perf/cost for 28k context and propose runtime config (kernel flags, sharding)
4) lucy.salesops: draft reserved + hosted pricing options
5) anita.sec: security preflight checklist + list of docs we need

mike.ae: Got it. Scheduling a sync with AquilaEdge Thurs 10am PT. I will post artifacts and kv-shape outputs here before the call. :calendar: 

kms-bot: KMS request created: request-8421 — onboarding link: https://kms.redwood/request/8421

devon.infra: Note — CMK onboarding typically ~3 business days. If they can’t export tokenizer, conversion step adds ~2–3 days to timeline and we should expect extra QA. Also for int8, plan calibration step in POC.

mike.ae: Thanks all — I’ll follow up with the artifact and ask them to run the snippet today. :thumbsup:
